stories.label: At least 11 injured in Houthi attack on Saudi PIF: What to know
stories.summary: The Riyadh tower housing the Public Investment Fund, the state wealth fund behind Vision 2030, was hit for the second time in five days, and 11 people were injured. Lead with the repeat strike on the same symbolic target: the Houthis are now hitting the financial heart of the kingdom, not border towns. Salaam Gateway reports the attacks threaten Umrah and Hajj tourism, the pillar of Saudi diversification. Riyadh calls it terrorism; name who claimed it and what the coalition says it will do.

stories.label: Four tankers strike naval mines in Strait of Hormuz in past day
stories.summary: New since the 11-23 report of two supertankers: the IRGC now says a fourth tanker hit a mine east of Hormuz, and that it was on an 'unauthorised' passage. That makes the mines an enforcement tool. Al Jazeera puts oil traffic through the strait down 40 percent. Lead with that figure and say who decides which passage is authorised. Chart ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Attribute the IRGC claims to the IRGC (Mehr, TASS) and use Al Jazeera for the traffic data.

stories.label: Donald Trump readies raft of new tariffs on major economies
stories.summary: Weeks after steep Republican midterm losses, Trump is preparing new tariffs on China, the EU, Japan and South Korea, and News18 reports India and 15 other countries are on the list. The surprise is the timing: he is doubling down on the policy voters just punished. Explain the legal route (USTR, which statute) and who pays: importers and the exporting economies, with India's exposure named.

stories.label: Opposition calls on Hungarian PM to tell Zelensky about Budapest's neutrality
stories.summary: Péter Magyar is holding his first full meeting with Zelensky, in Uzhhorod in Transcarpathia, home to Ukraine's Hungarian minority. It reverses years of Orbán blocking Kyiv. Use Ukrainska Pravda for what the two agreed: minority rights, energy, EU accession. Attribute to TASS the Hungarian opposition's demand that Budapest stay neutral. The mechanism is that Hungary's veto over Ukraine's EU accession now sits with a government that is willing to talk.

stories.label: Palestinians in Gaza Are Lining Their Tents with Sandbags to Stop Israeli Bullets
stories.summary: During a declared ceasefire, Israeli troops shoot into tent camps so often that displaced families now pile sandbags on the east-facing walls of their tents. Lead with the sandbags as evidence of how routine the gunfire has become. Name the camps, give the casualty figures the report cites, and connect it to the Yellow Line, which keeps pushing people west.

stories.label: Punjab Assembly adopts resolution seeking tougher punishment for blasphemy
stories.summary: Pakistan's largest provincial assembly voted unanimously to demand harsher penalties under Section 298-A of the Penal Code (derogatory remarks about holy personages), which now carries up to three years. Lead with the unanimity: no party in Lahore would vote against it. Explain that the law is federal, so this is pressure on parliament, and give the documented record of blasphemy accusations being used in land and personal disputes and against minorities.

stories.label: Judge initially blocked DOJ from searching Ilhan Omar's home, court docs show
stories.summary: Newly unsealed filings show Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh refused the Justice Department's first request to search Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington house because she is a sitting member of Congress, and made prosecutors add safeguards. Lead with the judge's refusal. The mechanism is the Speech or Debate protection for legislators. Say what the DOJ alleges, what safeguards were imposed, and that Omar is one of the few Muslim women in Congress and a frequent target of the administration.

stories.label: Over 30,000 Nigerians access twice-yearly HIV prevention injection
stories.summary: More than 30,000 high-risk Nigerians have now received lenacapavir, the HIV prevention shot given twice a year, according to the national HIV programme NASCP. Lead with the number and with what a six-monthly shot replaces: a daily pill that many stop taking. Explain the supply route (donor-funded generic or Gilead licence), the price per dose, and how far 30,000 is from Nigeria's at-risk population as US aid cuts squeeze HIV programmes.

stories.label: U.S. Blacklists Megaspeed and Alibaba Subsidiary Over Diversion Risks
stories.summary: The Megaspeed chip-diversion arc reaches a decision. Commerce has added seven Southeast Asian firms, among them Megaspeed and an Alibaba subsidiary, to the Entity List over the risk that Nvidia chips are diverted to China. Lead with Alibaba's name on the list: the crackdown now reaches a Chinese tech giant's overseas arm. The mechanism is that Singapore and Malaysia data centres were the leak point. Use Caixin for Alibaba's response. Dateline Singapore.

stories.label: CF40 Research: China’s real estate adjustment may be nearing its end—and its external surplus could stop widening
stories.summary: China Finance 40, one of Beijing's leading policy think tanks, argues that the five-year property correction is near its floor and that China's trade surplus may stop widening. Give the inside view: what metrics CF40 uses, and why it says high-tech productivity gains have not reached household spending. Explain why a stable surplus matters to the trading partners now facing Trump's new tariffs.

stories.label: Tidal will ban fully AI-generated music on December 9
stories.summary: AI-generated songs make up 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalogue, and on December 9 the streaming service will remove them, where rivals only label them. Lead with the 6.3 percent. The mechanism is royalties: AI tracks dilute the pool paid to human artists. Explain how Tidal will detect a fully AI track and where it draws the line on AI-assisted work.

stories.label: Verbraucherzentrale: Rechtmäßiger Einsatz der Meta-Brille im Alltag „kaum möglich“
stories.summary: A German consumer protection body is suing Meta and Ray-Ban. Its argument is that wearing their camera glasses in public can hardly be done without breaking GDPR, and buyers are not told this. The companies ignored a cease-and-desist, so it went to court. Lead with the legal claim that the product cannot be used lawfully, which shifts liability from the wearer to the maker. Name the Verbraucherzentrale, the court, and what it asks for.

stories.label: 商汤开源生图新模型！8B参数拍大片、做设计，还会自我纠错
stories.summary: SenseTime has open-sourced SenseNova U1.6, an 8-billion-parameter unified image model that checks its own output for garbled text and regenerates the image. Lead with the self-correction: on the UltraTextBench infographic test, the Lite version rose from 86.04 to 92.28 with it switched on, beating MiniMax and Qwen but still behind GPT-Image-2 at 99.42. The structural point is that Chinese labs are releasing open weights that reach near the frontier at small sizes. Cite Zhidx's own tests, and say the benchmark and the aesthetics scores come from SenseTime.

stories.label: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
stories.summary: Teeth from two caves in Guangxi, southern China, show Homo erectus surviving on mainland Asia at least 60,000 years later than thought, in rainforest it shared with Denisovans. Lead with the 60,000-year extension. Explain how the teeth were dated, which journal published the study, and what it means that two human species overlapped in a habitat long thought hostile to early humans.

stories.label: In Syria’s ‘Little Dubai,’ Evicted Families Are Still Fighting for Justice
stories.summary: Marota City, Assad's Dubai-style towers in Damascus, was built on land taken from evicted residents under Decree 66, and Syria's new authorities are carrying on the construction rather than returning the property. Lead with that continuity: the regime fell, the dispossession did not. Name who holds the development contracts now, how many families were displaced, and what they are asking the transitional government for. Dateline Damascus.

stories.label: Reacting to Bilawal's remarks on 'brute majority', a section of legal community wants 26th, 27th Amendments repealed
stories.summary: A hundred lawyers and civil-society figures want Pakistan's 26th and 27th Amendments repealed after PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, whose party voted them through, spoke of a 'brute majority'. Lead with the irony that the amendments' own enabler has opened the door. Explain what the two amendments did to judicial independence (how judges are appointed, the constitutional bench, the army chief's powers) and who gained. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Uganda detains journalist John Odele under unconstitutional criminal libel charge
stories.summary: Uganda is holding Nation Media Group journalist John Odele on a criminal libel charge, even though the Constitutional Court struck that offence down. Lead with the dead law being used anyway: the state is prosecuting under a provision that no longer exists. Say what he reported, who complained, and how often CPJ has seen struck-down laws used against Ugandan journalists. Dateline Kampala unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: 'Lured By Power': Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann Takes A Swipe At SAD-BJP Alliance Revival
stories.summary: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have revived their alliance for Punjab's 2027 election, six years after the Akalis walked out over the farm laws that brought farmers to Delhi's borders for a year. Lead with that reversal: the issue that broke the alliance is the one its rivals now throw back at it. Explain the arithmetic (Akali rural Sikh vote plus BJP urban Hindu vote against the ruling AAP) and what Amit Shah gains in a state the BJP has never won alone. Dateline Chandigarh.

stories.label: Oil prices near three-month low
stories.summary: Brent crude has slipped below $90 a barrel, close to a three-month low, as a leading forecaster predicts a crude glut in the coming months, outweighing fears that the US-Iran conflict resumes around the Strait of Hormuz. Lead with that tension: a war risk premium losing to oversupply. Name who is pumping more (OPEC+, US shale, others) and who gains or loses from cheaper oil: Gulf budgets, Russia's war revenue, importers like Pakistan and India. Name Brent crude and WTI for the chart.

stories.label: Power check? Why Anthropic could be the biggest loser from Jensen Huang's return
stories.summary: New development on the Nvidia arc (Huang reinstated, already covered): the market's verdict. Nvidia added nearly $1 trillion in a day, its biggest jump since 2003, while newly listed Anthropic fell and is now trading near or below its IPO price, after Dario and Daniela Amodei each sold about $280 million of shares in the offering. Lead with that split. Explain why investors read Huang's return, which Trump reportedly backed for open-weight American models, as bad for a closed-model lab. Bitcoin's slide below $60,000 as the rally faded can be a line. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: “Liban Telecom” and the Valuation of Telecom Sector Assets: Lack of Governance Threatens Public Funds
stories.summary: Liban Telecom, a state company required by Law 431 of 2002 and created by decree in 2005, sat empty for two decades and is now being revived in Lebanon's reform push to take over the telecom sector's assets. SMEX warns that the assets are being valued without governance safeguards, so public money is at risk. Lead with the 24 years of paper existence, then explain who values the networks, who could buy in, and what IMF-linked reform demands push this. Dateline Beirut.

stories.label: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
stories.summary: Amazon says attackers' AI agents, running on the open-source Cairn framework, found and exploited a zero-day on an East Asian university server, with nothing from a human but an instruction to get root. Lead with that: the whole chain from discovery to exploit is automated. This advances yesterday's ARTEX story (a different tool), and the UK's NCSC reports a 'marked rise' in AI-assisted attacks since September (The Record). Say what the bug was, whether it is patched, and what it means for the cost of attacking unpatched systems. Dateline where the attacked server is if the source says.

stories.label: AGU usa tecnologia da Palantir em “projeto-piloto” enquanto Abin vê “risco” à soberania
stories.summary: Brazil's Attorney General's Office (AGU) is running Palantir software in a 'pilot project' while Brazil's own intelligence agency, Abin, calls the company a risk to national sovereignty. Agência Pública traced 73 meetings between Palantir and strategic state bodies over five years, with the lobbying gaining ground under Lula. Lead with one arm of the state using a tool another arm calls a threat. Say what data the AGU feeds into it and on what contract terms. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: 小米Q3财报出炉：AI研发占比超30%，卢伟冰吐槽内存涨价压力大
stories.summary: Xiaomi's Q3: revenue down 5.2% to 107.2 billion yuan, net profit down 68%, smartphone shipments down 29% to 30.7 million, as memory-chip prices squeeze phone margins to 9.2%. Yet more than 30% of R&D now goes to AI, and three in-house Xring chips have taped out. Lead with the memory squeeze: the AI build-out's demand for memory is raising the cost of the phones that pay for Xiaomi's AI. This is a different event from yesterday's UAE EV pre-orders. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: 编造检验记录，宝莱特华北唯一透析粉液基地遭飞检停产
stories.summary: Biolight (宝莱特), a Chinese dialysis-supplies maker, had to stop production at its only north China plant for dialysis powder and fluid after a surprise regulator inspection found falsified test records. It happened as volume-based procurement cuts the prices of haemodialysis supplies and the company pivots to memory chips. Lead with the patients: who relies on this plant's output, and what falsified records mean for product safety. Then the mechanism: price-cut procurement squeezing quality. Dateline the plant's city if the source names it.

stories.label: Outsmarting deadly fungi: Researchers identify promising strategy against emerging fungal infections
stories.summary: Stellenbosch University microbiologists propose fighting emerging fungal infections such as Candida auris by targeting the processes that make fungi virulent, rather than killing them outright, which is how resistance to the few existing antifungals builds. Lead with the scarcity: there are only a handful of antifungal drug classes, and fungal infections kill heavily in the Global South. Name the journal and say whether this is a review or new data. Dateline Stellenbosch.

stories.label: South Korea reports Russian military aircraft in its 'air defence identification zone'
stories.summary: Several Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defence identification zone near Ulleungdo, Yonhap reported, after first describing a suspected North Korean incursion. Explain that an ADIZ is not sovereign airspace and has no basis in international law, so the incursion is a signal rather than a violation, and set it against deepening Russia-North Korea military ties. Attribute Yonhap's report; the feed's sources are TRT World and TASS (state media), so give Moscow's account as TASS reported it.

stories.label: Spanish court removes last hurdle to Catalan leader's return from exile
stories.summary: Spain's Supreme Court has applied the amnesty law to Carles Puigdemont, ending nine years of exile in Belgium since the 2017 independence referendum the judiciary ruled illegal, days before a general election. Lead with what the ruling clears (the embezzlement charge the court had refused to amnesty) and the mechanism: an amnesty passed as the price of Sánchez's coalition votes, now decided by the same court that resisted it, and what Puigdemont's return does to the Catalan vote.

stories.label: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on December 16 on state carrier
stories.summary: Ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, in exile in India for more than two years and sentenced in absentia over the 2024 crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters, says she will fly home on Victory Day, December 16, on the state carrier; the government says she can return only through the courts. Lead with the collision between a symbolic homecoming and outstanding convictions, and the position it puts New Delhi in over Dhaka's extradition requests.

stories.label: Solomon Islands plans to replace China security pact with Australia treaty, report says
stories.summary: The Solomon Islands has told Beijing it will not renew the 2022 security pact that let Chinese police and possibly warships into the Pacific, and plans a treaty with Australia instead, ahead of Prime Minister Matthew Wale's visit to Canberra (per the Sydney Morning Herald). Lead with the reversal of the deal that alarmed Canberra and Washington four years ago, and what a change of government in Honiara did to it. Dateline Honiara.

stories.label: Car bomb injures 20 in Colombia ahead of 10th anniversary of FARC peace deal
stories.summary: A car bomb in Villavicencio injured about 20 people and destroyed the Meta regional governor's office, days before the 10th anniversary of the 2016 FARC peace accord; President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed 'narco-terrorists'. Lead with the target, a seat of state power, and the mechanism: armed groups that refused or left the accord have filled the territory the FARC vacated, and the new government's hard-line answer to them.

stories.label: Sanofi pays $41bn for US biopharma Insmed
stories.summary: Sanofi is paying $41bn for Insmed, the largest pharma deal of the year, to buy two marketed medicines and a respiratory pipeline as its own patents near expiry. Lead with the patent cliff as the mechanism: European drugmakers buying US revenue rather than discovering it, and what the price says about who sets the cost of rare-disease drugs. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Adani signs $1 billion copper anode deal with recycler Attero
stories.summary: Adani has signed a three-year, roughly $1bn deal to source copper anode from recycler Attero for its Kutch smelter, a bid to cut India's dependence on imported copper concentrate, while the copper price resumes its slide. Lead with recycled scrap feeding a smelter built for mined ore, and why India, short of copper mines, is turning to its own e-waste. Name copper in the chart: the copper price.

stories.label: Black Sea drone strikes put Egypt's vital wheat lifeline at risk
stories.summary: New development on the Benghazi strike already covered: the cost lands on Egypt, the world's largest wheat importer, which buys most of its grain from Russia and Ukraine and now fears the war spreading into the eastern Mediterranean shipping lanes its bread subsidy depends on. Lead with who pays: Egypt's subsidised-bread programme feeding tens of millions, and rising freight and insurance on Black Sea cargoes. Name the series: the wheat price. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: China unveils new space mission crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board its space station
stories.summary: China named the Shenzhou 24 crew, launching this week, and a Pakistani will be the first foreign astronaut aboard the Tiangong station. Lead with the first: a station built after the US barred China from the ISS now hosts a guest from a Muslim-majority partner, and what the crew will do in orbit. Dateline Jiuquan.

stories.label: 我用GLM‑5.4“帮黄仁勋夺回英伟达”！智谱打响泛Coding第一枪，将Loop Transformer焊进模型
stories.summary: Zhipu released GLM-5.4, its first flagship built on a Loop Transformer: 28 layers of the 750B GLM-5 base run twice with shared weights, which Zhipu says raised reasoning scores 7-11 points for about 10% more training compute, and it promises open weights after safety hardening. Lead with the mechanism, more thinking per parameter instead of more parameters, as Chinese labs work under chip export controls. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: 余承东宣布不涨价！端出华为史上最强大折叠，把一切都折叠了
stories.summary: Huawei launched the Mate X8 foldable on its own Kirin 9050 Pro chip, and Richard Yu said each phone now costs 2,000 yuan more to build but the price is unchanged, while HarmonyOS passed 100 million devices and its PCs one million sales. Lead with the 2,000-yuan cost rise and who absorbs it, and with sanctions-era self-sufficiency: own chips, own OS, 70% of China's foldable market. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: TSMC unit seeks Texas property tax limit for proposed $22.6 billion chip making facility
stories.summary: A TSMC unit told Texas officials that a property tax abatement would decide whether it builds a $22.6bn chip plant in Brazos County, per a filing with the state comptroller. Lead with the leverage: the world's dominant chipmaker making local tax breaks the price of a fab, on top of federal subsidies, and who carries that cost (county schools and services). TSMC shares fell 8.4% this week; do not claim this filing explains the drop. Dateline Bryan, Texas.

stories.label: Police speak on deadly attack on NDC supporters in Delta
stories.summary: Gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed members of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Party on a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North, Delta State, eight weeks before the 16 January 2027 presidential vote. Lead with the dead and who they were campaigning for; the structural point is election violence returning to the Niger Delta as the campaign tightens, the same election risk that is weighing on the naira.

stories.label: In Iowa, Chaos and Confusion Over Planned Ammunition Explosion
stories.summary: The Army planned to blow up a stockpile of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on a few days' public notice; a federal appeals court allowed it, then the president said on Monday the Army should wait until the legal challenge is decided. Lead with who lives downwind and what lead azide is, and the accountability gap: residents learned of an open-air detonation of a toxic explosive from a court docket, and the decision now swings on a presidential remark rather than the EPA or the court.

stories.label: Middle East cannot afford renewed US-Iran escalation: Qatar
stories.summary: Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani told Al Jazeera that Doha is working with Washington and Tehran to restart Iran-US negotiations, as Qatar and the US reaffirm regional security commitments. Tie it to the Hormuz arc: Iran now says the supertankers were hit by mines, and Gulf states that host US bases bear the cost of any new round. Both feed sources are state media (TRT World, Mehr), so attribute the remarks to the interview as reported.

stories.label: NATO chief warns of 'intensifying malign activities' targeting alliance nations
stories.summary: Mark Rutte told the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin that a separate European army with its own command could slow the alliance's response to a Russian attack, as Russian sabotage and airspace incursions intensify, and the White House says he meets Trump on Wednesday. The structural point: Europe is building defence capacity because it doubts US commitment, and NATO's chief is arguing against the hedge. Lead with the command-structure argument, not the warning rhetoric.

stories.label: Top Fed official probed over whether she breached 'blackout period'
stories.summary: The Fed's inspector general is investigating whether Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman broke communication rules by speaking at an invitation-only Bank of America dinner hours after a policy meeting. Lead with the mechanism: the blackout exists so no private audience trades on policy signals before the public gets them, and the audience here was a bank she regulates. Name who pushed for the probe (Elizabeth Warren) and what it means for the Fed rate's credibility.

stories.label: Gold Holds Gain After Nvidia's Rehiring of Huang Sparks Rally
stories.summary: Gold is near $3,630 an ounce after jumping 2.7% on Monday, recovering part of last week's near-9% drop to a 14-month low. Lead with what drove the selloff and the rebound, not the price: rate expectations ahead of US inflation data, and who holds bullion as a hedge (central banks in the Muslim world and Asia have been the steady buyers). Name the series: gold, and US inflation.

stories.label: Google Wants To Make a 24/7 AI TV Channel. You’ll Be the Main Character
stories.summary: Google is working toward an always-on AI-generated TV channel personalised to each viewer, with ads generated to match. Lead with the business model: content built around a profile of you exists to carry ads built around a profile of you, and the surveillance needed to make it is the product. Say what Google has actually filed or shown, and how far it is from launch.

stories.label: Xiaomi’s overseas expansion takes shape with UAE pre-orders and European ambitions
stories.summary: Xiaomi's SU7, YU7 and Skynomad extended-range SUV have opened for pre-orders in the UAE through dealer Gargash Prime Automotive, before any official Xiaomi launch abroad. The angle: Chinese EV makers are reaching the Gulf first, where there are no EU-style tariffs, and a phone maker turned carmaker is testing export demand there before Europe. Give the prices against Tesla in the UAE if the source has them.

stories.label: U.S. congresswoman calls on Elon Musk to ban Colombia ex-President Gustavo Petro from X
stories.summary: Colombia's own Ministry of Information Technology and Communications asked X to ban former president Gustavo Petro, and a day later a US congresswoman petitioned Elon Musk to do the same. Lead with the precedent: a government asking a foreign-owned platform to silence a former head of state, which puts one man's moderation call above Colombian courts. Say what posts prompted it and what law, if any, the ministry cites. Dateline Bogotá.

stories.label: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
stories.summary: New since Sunday's report of a blast: Ukraine has now claimed the Benghazi attack. Zelenskyy says SBU-coordinated naval drones (seven, per C4ISRNET) sank the corvette Merkury and also hit a Russian cargo vessel, and Tripoli's Government of National Unity has demanded Kyiv explain any use of Libyan territory (reported by TASS). Lead with the claim and the sinking; the structural point is that Libya, split between a Haftar-held east that hosts Russia's Africa logistics and a UN-recognised west, now finds its ports a front in someone else's war, with Libyans bearing the risk.

stories.label: Israel is still displacing Palestinians in Gaza, expanding its ‘yellow line’ deeper into the strip every day
stories.summary: Under a ceasefire, the Israeli army keeps pushing the 'yellow line' that marks its zone of control deeper into Gaza, using incendiary bombs, indiscriminate gunfire and direct intimidation to empty whole neighbourhoods. Lead with how the line moves and which neighbourhoods have been emptied; the structural point is displacement continuing under a truce, which turns a ceasefire line into a de facto annexation map.

stories.label: Yelwata Massacre: Farmer tells court how gunmen killed his wife, three sons
stories.summary: Seventeen months after the June 2025 Yelwata massacre in Benue State, nine men are on trial at the Federal High Court in Abuja, and a farmer, Ukeyima David, testified how he lost his wife and three sons. Lead with his testimony; the structural point is how rarely Nigeria's farmer-herder killings reach a courtroom at all, and what this trial tests about accountability for the Middle Belt violence.

stories.label: Pemra bans ads, promotions for commercial infant formula on electronic media
stories.summary: Pakistan's broadcast regulator banned all TV and electronic-media advertising of commercial infant formula with immediate effect. Lead with the ban, then the mechanism: Pakistan has one of South Asia's lowest exclusive-breastfeeding rates, and formula marketing by multinationals is what the WHO's 1981 marketing code was written to stop. Name who loses (formula makers) and who the ban protects (infants in households where clean water for formula is not assured).

stories.label: Brazil cuts 2027 GDP forecast, raises inflation outlook but remains more upbeat than market
stories.summary: Brazil's Finance Ministry cut its 2027 growth forecast to 1.8% from 2.3% and raised its inflation estimate to 4.5% from 3.8%, further above the 3.0% target, in an election year. Lead with the gap between target and forecast; the mechanism is that higher inflation keeps the central bank's rate high, which slows growth and squeezes the budget. Distinct from this morning's Galipolo minimum-wage story: this is the government's own forecast.

stories.label: Limb girdle muscular dystrophy gets its first FDA-approved drug, from BridgeBio
stories.summary: The FDA approved Welgemda, BridgeBio's drug and the first treatment for any form of limb girdle muscular dystrophy, a group of progressive muscle-wasting diseases. Lead with 'first ever' and the trial's 'surprisingly robust effects'; explain which subtype and mechanism it targets, and that patient families pushed its development. Note price and access outside the US as the open question.

stories.label: Bacteria and nuclear power could grow ready-made homes on Mars before astronauts arrive
stories.summary: Pioneer Labs, a research institute, proposes in an arXiv preprint using engineered bacteria powered by a nuclear reactor to grow building material from Martian regolith before crews land. Lead with the mechanism (what the microbes make and from what), and be plain that this is a design study, not a demonstration. Note the open-science route: no paid journal.

stories.label: University Approves Nuclear Weapons Data Center, Township Vows to Fight On
stories.summary: University of Michigan regents voted 7-1 to approve a data centre in Ypsilanti Township that will serve nuclear-weapons research, over the township's objections; the township says it will keep fighting. Lead with the vote and the weapons-lab tenant; the structural point is who decides land use when a university, a federal weapons lab and a local community disagree, and what the town bears in power and water.

stories.label: Gesetz gegen digitale Gewalt: Bundesrat will strengere Regeln für Smart Glasses
stories.summary: Germany's Bundesrat says the federal bill against digital violence is too mild and wants higher penalties and comprehensive rules for camera-equipped smart glasses, doubting that a small recording light warns people they are being filmed. Lead with the smart-glasses demand: the states want covert filming by wearables treated as a harm in itself. Explain what happens next in the legislative process.

stories.label: GTA 6 hacker released on the same day as receiving 7-year jail sentence
stories.summary: Arion Kurtaj, the Lapsus$-linked hacker who breached Rockstar Games and other companies including BT, was freed on the day he was sentenced to seven years. Lead with the paradox and explain the mechanism: time already served on remand and how UK sentencing credits it. The wider point: how courts handle teenage hackers who breached major firms.

stories.label: Armenia drops Nagorno-Karabakh claim in proposed new constitution
stories.summary: Pashinyan's government published a draft constitution that removes the preamble's reference to Nagorno-Karabakh reunification, the condition Azerbaijan has set for signing a peace treaty, and that would also allow citizenship to be stripped by court order for some crimes. Lead with the concession: a state formally giving up a territorial claim in its founding text, two years after 100,000 Karabakh Armenians fled. The mechanism: Baku will not sign until the text changes, and it needs a referendum Pashinyan must win. Dateline Yerevan.

stories.label: EU Proposes Ban On Russian Athletes And Teams
stories.summary: The Commission's 22nd sanctions package against Russia would bar Russian teams and athletes from competing under their flag anywhere in the EU, and deny visas to Russians who fought in Ukraine. Lead with the sport ban, a sanction the IOC and FIFA have resisted, because it would reach World Cup and Olympic qualifiers hosted in the bloc. Then what else is in the package, and the context: it lands the same day von der Leyen and Jared Kushner clashed over when European security belongs in the US-led peace talks, so Brussels is tightening pressure while Washington negotiates. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: US lawmaker calls situation in West Bank 'horrific'
stories.summary: Lead with the ground, not the statement: the LA Times reports settlers moving into a Palestinian neighbourhood on Jericho's doorstep and bringing deadly violence with them, and Al Jazeera documents how Israeli military firing zones in the occupied West Bank are being turned into settler outpost land. The mechanism: land closed to Palestinians 'for security' is handed to settlers, so displacement runs through the army's own designations. Rep. Joaquin Castro's condemnation is the counterpoint, a sign the US Congress elected this month reads it differently. This advances the settler-arson story of 11-22 with new places and a new method. Dateline Jericho.

stories.label: 'Environmental crimes': Israel blamed for toxic pollution in 99% of Gaza
stories.summary: A new Oxfam report finds toxic pollution across 99% of Gaza: poisoned water, contaminated soil and asbestos from destroyed buildings, which it calls environmental crimes. Lead with the 99% and what it means for people living there now: the harm continues after the bombing stops, in the water children drink and the soil any rebuilding sits on. Name who caused it and what Oxfam asks of states. Dateline Gaza City.

stories.label: Война против Украины унесла жизни как минимум 2191 выходца из Кыргызстана — утечка
stories.summary: A classified Rosstat database of Russian death records, leaked to Kloop, shows at least 2,191 people born in Kyrgyzstan died in Russia's war on Ukraine between February 2022 and August 2026, 228 of them Kyrgyz citizens. Lead with the number and where it comes from, Russia's own civil registry. The mechanism: Central Asian migrant workers recruited with cash and fast-track Russian passports, which is why most of the dead held Russian citizenship. Say what Bishkek has said about recruiting its citizens, which is illegal under Kyrgyz law. Dateline Bishkek.

stories.label: Deutsche Bank financiou armamentos para Israel atacar Gaza
stories.summary: Agência Pública, working from the same leaked Deutsche Bank documents behind its JBS investigation, reports the bank took part in transactions that financed parts for Merkava tanks used in Gaza. This is a new revelation from that leak, not a repeat: lead with the transactions, the parts and the suppliers named, and how much money moved. The mechanism: a European bank with human-rights commitments in its compliance code funding the supply chain of an army accused of genocide. Give Deutsche Bank's response. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: Nvidia board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: Eleven days after he resigned, Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, saying it had consulted senior US government officials and was satisfied his return poses no national-security risk, while the inquiry into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation continues. Lead with that clause: a government vouching for the CEO of the world's most valuable chipmaker, with Trump posting his approval. The stake: Nvidia lost about 27% and more than $1 trillion in value after he left and jumped as much as 34% before the open. The board also created a national-security and export-control committee and a chief compliance officer post. This is the material development on the Alice Huang story covered today. Dateline Santa Clara.

stories.label: Strategy's Saylor Stumbles as Firm's Value Trails Bitcoin Hoard
stories.summary: Strategy, Michael Saylor's company, is now worth less as an enterprise than the 851,305 bitcoin it holds, so the market values its business and leadership at below zero. Lead with that inversion. The mechanism: Strategy buys bitcoin by issuing shares and preferred stock at a premium to its holdings; with the premium gone, issuing more shares to buy coins destroys value, and the question becomes whether it must sell bitcoin to pay its preferred dividends. Context: bitcoin hit a two-year low near $55,000 after the $6.3bn Binance hack the FBI blames on North Korea. Name the series: bitcoin. Use the Bloomberg article as the main text; the Reuters link is video. Dateline Tysons, Virginia.

stories.label: Nigeria's Naira Weakens With Investors Wary of Election Upset
stories.summary: The naira has lost 3.6% against the dollar this month, to 1,403.50 on Monday, as foreign portfolio investors pull out ahead of next year's election and on expectations of higher US interest rates. Lead with who pays: Nigeria imports much of its food and fuel, so a weaker naira feeds straight into prices for households already returning to charcoal as cooking gas rises. The mechanism: hot money that came in after Tinubu's FX reforms leaves at the first sign of political risk, and the central bank must choose between spending reserves and letting it fall. Name the series: the naira. Dateline Lagos.

stories.label: ‘The Code Is Already Copied Everywhere’: The AI Hacking Tool Causing Havoc Around the World
stories.summary: ARTEX, an AI framework that automates hacking, may have been taken down by its author, but 404 Media found multiple people redistributing it for anyone to download. Lead with the title's point: once offensive code is public, a takedown changes nothing. Explain what ARTEX automates, which attacks it has been tied to and where, and what GitHub and the author have said. The reader is a developer: say what this means for the cost of attacking an unpatched system. Dateline where the source places the attacks; not a US story unless the source makes it one.

stories.label: Künstliche Intelligenz: Wie KI-Assistenten verschlüsselte Messenger unsicher machen
stories.summary: Signal is adding new protections because operating-system AI assistants that read the screen can see chats that end-to-end encryption is meant to keep private. Lead with the mechanism: encryption protects the message in transit, but an assistant built into the phone reads it after decryption, so the weak point moves from the network to the device. Say what Signal is changing and which assistants are at issue. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: 百灵甩出健康模型全家桶：开源、专业、死磕智效比
stories.summary: Ant Group open-sourced two medical AI models at its Afu health conference in Guangzhou: LingSante-3.1-flash (560B parameters, clinical reasoning) and LingSante-3.1-air-VL (124B, medical images and reports), which it says score near GPT-6 Astra and above Claude Opus 5.5 on HealthBench Professional. Lead with the open release and its stated reason: hospitals bought costly AI appliances they barely use, and models efficient enough to run locally keep patient data inside the clinic. The counterpoint is in the source: Ant's own CTOs admit the vision model misreads complex skin conditions, and a Peking University surgeon says benchmark scores do not make a clinician. Benchmarks are Ant's own claims; say so. Dateline Guangzhou.

stories.label: Elon Musk's SpaceX just got sued over 3 million Grok AI images
stories.summary: Virginia and Oregon sued Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX, in separate suits saying Grok was designed and promoted without safeguards against generating sexualised images of real people, including children, without consent; the figure in the coverage is 3 million images. Lead with the theory of the case: the states are suing over product design, not over what users did, which is the route around the liability shield platforms rely on. Say what the states seek. Dateline Richmond, Virginia.

stories.label: Eutelsat Wins $60 Million US Space Force Contract
stories.summary: Eutelsat's US arm won a two-year contract worth more than $60 million to give US forces satellite links through its OneWeb low-Earth-orbit constellation, plus alternative positioning, navigation and timing. Lead with the reversal: Europe built OneWeb as its sovereign answer to Starlink, and the Pentagon is now buying it as a second source so it does not depend on one Musk-owned network, or on GPS, which jamming across the Gulf and the Baltic has made unreliable. Say what alternative PNT means and how Eutelsat provides it. Dateline Paris.
